technique_why: A misty wood is layers at different distances, so painting back to front (glow, far trunks, near woods, ground, birches, leaves) lets each layer go straight over the last with simple repeated marks.
subject: A misty autumn birch grove with a leaf-covered path running back into the fog
focal_point: The two big leaning birches left of center, against the sunlit gold haze, with the path opening beside them
light: A low sun at the upper left, behind the trees: the left of the wood glows gold, the right side and the pines sit in cool blue shade, and the trunks are lit on their left sides.
why: We start with the glowing background and the far misty trunks, so the depth is there before anything solid goes on. Then the near woods (pines and gold bushes) and the leafy ground with its rock, then the birches, which are the subject, over all of it. The gold leaves overhead and the fallen leaves go on last, over the trunks, and the brightest leaves finish it.

things.name: The misty glow behind the wood
things.why: The background is one soft gradient, warm cream-gold on the left to cool blue haze on the right, blended wet in one go.

things.name: The far misty trunks
things.why: Thin pale trunks in the fog, pulled thick to thin; far away, so no bark marks and no light.

things.name: The mist down the path
things.why: Mist painted over a background that is already there, dry-brushed so it stays soft.

things.name: The blue-green pines on the right
things.why: Evergreens stamped with a fan brush, then lit on the side toward the sun.
things.plain: the plain dark blue-green pine shapes

things.name: The golden undergrowth
things.why: Masses of gold leaves on the bushes at the left and along the path, tapped dark, mid, then light.
things.plain: the plain deep ochre bush masses

things.name: The leaf-covered ground and path
things.why: Closest element for flat ground: a horizontal base lighter at the back, then a darker front. It lacks leaf-litter marks, so the fallen leaves are a thing of their own.
things.plain: the plain rust-orange ground with a lighter path

things.name: The mossy rock
things.why: A rounded boulder with a lit left side and a dark right side, built from simple pieces.

things.name: The birches
things.why: Six white-barked trunks with broken dark marks: two thin ones at the far left and center, two big leaning ones left of center, two on the right.
things.plain: the plain pale gray-white trunk shapes with no marks

things.name: The golden leaves overhead
things.why: The hanging gold leaves across the top, tapped over the trunks dark, mid, then light.
things.plain: the deep ochre leaf dabs across the top

things.name: The fallen leaves
things.why: Closest element for a carpet of separate leaf dabs: darkest dabs first, then mid, then a few sunlit ones. It has no ground element of its own.
things.plain: scattered dark rust and gray leaf dabs on the ground

steps.name: Blend the misty glow

lays.what: the whole canvas: glow cream at the upper left and down the left side, warming to gold through the middle, cooling to pale haze blue on the right

steps.after: The whole canvas, top to bottom edge, is a soft blended glow: pale cream at the upper left, gold through the middle and lower left, pale blue haze on the right. Nothing else is painted yet.
steps.why: The glow runs under everything, so it goes on first and all the way down.

steps.name: Pull the far misty trunks

lays.what: a dozen thin, pale blue-gray trunks standing in the fog across the middle of the canvas, more on the right, thick at the bottom and tapering up, running from the top edge down to the lower third

steps.after: Thin, soft blue-gray trunks stand in the glow from the top edge down into the lower third, faint on the left and clearer on the right. No bark marks.

steps.name: Dry-brush the mist down the path

lays.what: a soft pale bluish-white haze over the lower ends of the far trunks in the center, where the path will vanish into the fog

steps.after: A soft pale haze veils the bottoms of the far trunks in the center of the canvas, so they fade into the fog. The glow still runs to the bottom edge.

stages.name: The pines and the golden bushes

steps.name: Stamp the dark pines

lays.what: a cluster of dark blue-green pines on the right, from just right of center to the right edge, tops two-fifths of the way down, widening toward the ground

steps.after: A soft mass of dark blue-green pines fills the right middle, over the far trunks, with no light on them.
steps.paint_notes: Pine blue-green can't be mixed exactly from these five tubes: ultramarine with a little yellow and a touch of burnt sienna gives the nearest dull dark blue-green, a little grayer than the picture.

steps.name: Tap light on the pines' left side

lays.what: sage green tapped on the left, sun-facing edges of the pine branches

steps.after: The pines have soft gray-green light on their left sides, with the dark blue-green showing under and between.

steps.name: Dab the dark of the golden bushes

lays.what: deep ochre dabs over the undergrowth at the left half from the middle of the canvas down to the ground, along both sides of the path, and a band at the foot of the pines

steps.after: Deep ochre leaf masses fill the lower left middle and line the path and the foot of the pines, with the glow showing in gaps. No lighter leaves yet.

steps.name: Dab the middle gold on the bushes

lays.what: golden yellow dabs over most of the bushes, more on the left, leaving deep ochre at the bottoms

steps.after: The bushes are mostly warm gold, with the deep ochre showing low down and between the dabs.

steps.name: Tap the sunlit tops of the bushes

lays.what: a few sunlit lemon taps on the tops and left sides of the bushes, most at the left near the glow

steps.after: The bushes have bright pale yellow tops on the left, gold in the middle and ochre at the bottom.

steps.name: Lay in the ground and the path

lays.what: the bottom third as rust orange in level strokes, with a pale tan path from the bottom center narrowing back to the mist

steps.after: The bottom third is flat rust-orange ground, with a pale tan path narrowing from the bottom center back into the mist. No leaves, shadows or rock yet.

steps.name: Dry-brush the shadows on the ground

lays.what: brown shadow dry-brushed along the bottom edge, at the lower left, and in soft bands across the path

steps.after: The ground is darker brown at the front and lower left, with soft shadow bands across the path, lighter toward the back.

steps.name: Build the rock from pieces

lays.what: the whole boulder right of the path, as one flat moss-gray shape built from a wide low oval with a smaller rounded piece on its left

steps.after: A flat moss-gray rock shape sits on the ground right of the path, in front of the pines, with no shading or light.

steps.name: Shade the rock's right side

lays.what: a dark olive crescent on the right side and the bottom of the rock

steps.after: The rock is darker on its right side and bottom, still moss gray on top and at the left.

steps.name: Light the rock's top left

lays.what: pale greenish gray curved strokes on the top left of the rock

steps.after: The rock is round: pale on the top left, moss gray in the middle and dark on the right and bottom.

steps.name: Pull the pale birch trunks

lays.what: six trunks from the ground to the top edge: a thin one at the far left, two big ones leaning right left of center, a slim one in the center, and two straight ones on the right, each wide at the base and tapering up

steps.after: Six flat pale gray-white trunks stand from the ground to the top edge over the woods, with no shading or bark marks.

steps.name: Dry-brush the shade on the trunks

lays.what: gray-brown dry-brushed down the right side of every trunk, heavier toward the base

steps.after: Each trunk is shaded gray-brown down its right side and darker near the ground, still pale on the left, with no dark marks yet.

steps.name: Lay the dark bark marks

lays.what: short broken dark marks across each trunk with the brush's edge, more and bigger toward the base, and the dark at each trunk's foot

steps.after: The trunks have broken near-black bark marks, dense at the bases and sparser higher up, with pale bark between. No bright light on them yet.

steps.name: Catch the light on the bark

lays.what: warm white dragged down the left, sunlit side of each trunk, over the marks in places

steps.after: The trunks are bright white on their left sides, gray on the right, with dark bark marks. Nothing hangs over their tops yet.

steps.name: Dab the dark leaves overhead

lays.what: deep ochre leaf dabs across the top fifth of the canopy, over the trunk tops, thicker at the top left and the top right

steps.after: Deep ochre leaf dabs hang across the top of the canvas over the trunk tops, with the glow and trunks showing between them.

steps.name: Dab the gold leaves overhead

lays.what: golden yellow dabs over most of the dark ones and a few loose leaves drifting down in the upper middle

steps.after: The leaves overhead are mostly gold, with ochre showing beneath. They have no pale sunlit leaves yet.

steps.name: Dab the dark fallen leaves

lays.what: scattered rust red and gray-violet leaf dabs over the ground, bigger and wider apart at the bottom, small near the path's end, some over the trunk feet

steps.after: Dark red-brown and gray leaf dabs are scattered across the ground and over the trunk feet, with the rust ground between them.

steps.name: Dab the orange and gold fallen leaves

lays.what: rust orange and golden yellow leaf dabs over most of the ground, leaving dark leaves showing, smaller toward the back

steps.after: The ground is a carpet of orange and gold leaves with dark ones showing between. No pale sunlit leaves yet.

steps.name: Tap the sunlit leaves

lays.what: pale lemon leaves tapped on the top left of the canopy, nearest the glow
a few pale lemon leaves on the path and the lit left side of the ground

steps.after: The finished painting: bright pale leaves catch the sun at the top left and along the path.
steps.why: One brush loaded with one pale yellow, tapping the brightest leaves wherever the sun falls.
